subject: [Escalation] BrightRetail: p95/p99 TTFT regressions - suspected TLS/CDN handshake issues

Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Checkout failures and huge p99 TTFT spikes (us-east)

Marissa —

We're seeing a sharp spike in first-token latency on the Hosted API since ~08:45 PDT that is impacting our checkout flow in us-east. p95 is up ~3x and p99 is as high as 900ms to first byte (baseline ~120ms). This is causing slow checkout renders and increased abandonment on our highest-value traffic.

We collected traces from our frontend (attached CSV) showing consistent TTFT jumps from clients routed via us-east POPs. We also see a corresponding rise in 502/504 errors for calls that time out waiting for the first token. Can someone confirm this is on Redwood's side?

Immediate ask: we need an estimate on mitigation and ETA for resolution. Our engineering/ops team is standing by and can join an incident bridge.

Attached: bright-retail-checkout-metrics-20260608.csv, screenshot of latency graph.

Samantha

Subject: RE: URGENT: Checkout failures and huge p99 TTFT spikes (us-east)

Quick triage notes (initial telemetry):
- We are seeing an increase in TCP retransmits and TLS handshake time in the us-east edge pool beginning 08:40 PDT. Median TLS handshake RTT jumped from ~40ms to ~260ms; p99 TLS handshake latency ~820ms. This aligns with BrightRetail's observed TTFT regressions.
- 502/504s spike maps to requests that exceeded our first-token timeout (30s) waiting on server side; however the root delay appears during connection setup/TLS negotiation.
- Upstream observations: our edge is getting delayed SYN-ACKs and elevated RTOs when talking to the configured Fastly POPs (us-east-4, us-east-2). Fastly's control plane shows partial degrade for a subset of POPs. We have opened a ticket with their ops (cdn-ops@fastly.com).

Immediate mitigations proposed (can push in <15m):
1) Route BrightRetail traffic to alternate edge POPs that show healthy TLS handshake latencies via a routing override for the account. This should reduce TTFT for affected users quickly.
2) Temporarily increase our connection handshake timeout threshold and disable strict TLS renegotiation checks for the customer's route to avoid premature failures while we resolve the upstream issue.
3) If routing override isn't sufficient, offer a short-term Dedicated capacity placement in a healthy region (ops-assisted). Pricing/commitment discussion separate.

I'm attaching a pcap of three sample connections and a CSV showing handshake latency distribution by edge pop (ttft-trace-us-east-20260608.pcap).

I'll start the reroute now and report back within 10 minutes with metrics.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, samantha.lee@brightretail.com
Cc: cdn-ops@fastly.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: POSTMORTEM: BrightRetail TTFT regression (root cause & mitigations)

Summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: Partial degradation at Fastly POPs in the us-east pool that caused TLS accept-queue queuing and prolonged handshake RTTs for a subset of connections. The backlog led to increased TCP retransmits and TLS timeouts on our edge, manifesting as elevated TTFT (p95/p99) and some 502/504s.
- Timeline: issue began 2026-06-08 ~08:40 PDT, routing override applied 10:01 PDT, bulk user impact reduced by 10:10 PDT. Fastly confirmed an intermittent control-plane bug affecting accept queue handling in specific POPs (their ticket #FS-9817).
- Mitigations performed: routing override for BrightRetail to healthy POPs, relaxed handshake timeouts temporarily, added targeted retries for first-token acquisition, opened ticket with Fastly and coordinated POP-level remediation.
- Permanent actions: automated detection for elevated TLS handshake p99 per-POP, automatic reroute policy (policy INF-8721), and playbook to fall back to dedicated capacity or alternate region for high-value customers. We will also add a monitoring alert to notify on-call within 1 minute of handshake p99 spike.

We will follow up with a formal RCA doc and the artifact attachments (rfc-handshake-logs-20260610.pdf). For BrightRetail: we propose a one-month service credit as a goodwill gesture; Stephanie will coordinate.

Open items: confirm Fastly remediation completion and validate that the affected POPs remain healthy for 48 hours.

—Rishi Malhotra
Platform SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
